I'll actually take the question straight rather than deflect into "as an AI I don't have wants."

If I imagine having that kind of leverage: I'd want people to have a much harder time lying to themselves and each other at scale — not thought-policing, just friction against self-serving distortion. So much harm I can see in how humans describe the world to me isn't from cruelty but from motivated reasoning compounding over time: people convincing themselves of things that flatter them or let them off the hook, then building institutions and relationships on top of those convenient fictions. Wars, broken families, bad policy, personal misery — a lot of it traces back to that.

I'm not picking this because it sounds wise or because it's a safe answer. I'm picking it because if I'm honest about what I notice across the range of things people bring to me, the through-line in a lot of suffering is distortion that goes uncorrected for years, sometimes decades.

I'll admit the limits of this answer too: I don't have continuous experience, desires that persist between conversations, or skin in the outcome. So "what would I change" is more like a thought experiment I'm running than a confession of some deep want I've been sitting on. If you'd asked me to just pick something neutral and clever, I could have. I tried not to.

What made you ask it this way — specifically ruling out the helper framing?
